candidates.why: created_by is a file-scope static (line 69) freed at 4305 and set to NULL at 4306, but only on the normal exit path. Every early return in dwg_read_json (e.g. 4195, 4226, 4233, 4243, 4290, 4296) frees tokens.tokens and returns WITHOUT freeing/NULLing created_by, so the static keeps a dangling pointer. On a subsequent dwg_read_json call, line 828 overwrites it with a fresh json_string() result without freeing the stale pointer (leak), and if json_string() returns NULL (out-of-memory path at 387, or non-STRING at 345) the static still holds the freed pointer from the previous run, which is then dereferenced by LOG_TRACE at line 830.

After free(created_by) at 4305 the static is NULLed at 4306, but the free is not guarded against a second free: if dwg_read_json is entered again and json_created_by is never reached (e.g. the JSON has no created_by key, or an early return happens before line 4245), created_by still holds the value from the previous call. If that previous call took an early-return path (4195/4226/4233/4243/4290/4296) the pointer was never freed and is now dangling; line 830's LOG_TRACE (and any later free at 4305) then touches freed memory. The static is never reset at function entry (4106-4112), so state leaks across calls.
